Appreciate the questions — answers below and I’ve linked the Redwood-verified perf profiles and the preliminary report. Full benchmark run scheduled for tomorrow with your final prompt set.

Summary (short):
- Recommended models for your QA workflow: 
  1) Redwood-13B-v1 (int8 quantized) — best cost/latency balance for multi-doc retrieval + answer synthesis. 
  2) Llama-2-70B-chat (FP16) — highest quality for long-context, higher cost and higher p95 latency.

- Performance highlights (based on our 1.5k token end-to-end prompt set; numbers are Redwood-verified, measured on our Dedicated G4dn-equivalent fleet):
  - Redwood-13B-v1 (int8): TPS (tokens/sec) = 320 ± 15, p50 latency (end-to-end) = 210 ms, p95 = 420 ms.
  - Llama-2-70B-chat (FP16): TPS = 85 ± 10, p50 = 640 ms, p95 = 1.1 s.
  - Note: numbers are for single-request concurrency at target seq len; batching and autoscale configs change TPS/p95 tradeoffs — we include a batch/latency curve in the report.

- Quality/regression guidance:
  - Int8 quantization for Redwood-13B-v1 has been validated on similar QA tasks. We typically observe negligible regression on F1/ROUGE metrics for retrieval-augmented QA when using our recommended calibration. For hallucination-sensitive flows we recommend running a prompt-level regression test (we can run on your production prompt set).
  - For high-sensitivity customer-facing responses, the 70B FP16 variant is safest, but cost ~3x and p95 ~2–3x higher vs. 13B quantized.

- Cost rough estimates for 10k QPM peak (back-of-envelope): assuming average response length ~300 tokens and Redwood-13B-v1 int8: ~9M tokens/day => monthly ~270M tokens. I’ll produce a detailed cost model and include Dedicated vs Hosted comparisons in the full deck.

Benchmark links & artifacts:
- Preliminary benchmark report: https://drive.redwood.ai/reports/ACME-2026-benchmarks
- Redwood-verified model profiles (summary table included in the report)
- Prompt set used for the run: attached (acme_prompt_set_v1.csv)

- I’ll schedule a 30m walkthrough of the results once the run completes (Thu preferred).

Hi Samantha — looping in as promised. Quick notes on rollout and evaluation that may help procurement/your SREs: 

- Canary/rollout suggestion: start with 5% traffic on Redwood-13B-v1 int8 for 72h, monitor token-level cost and p95 latency on the Redwood Console (we’ll share a per-route dashboard). If quality metrics are stable, move to 25% for 48h, then 100%.
- Regression and evals: we’ll push a diff report that compares NPS-like metrics (answer correctness, extraction F1) for the prompt set across variants; this surfaces small regressions early.
- Compliance note: if you need Private deployment (VPC) for logs/KMS, we can scope that in the procurement doc — I’ll await procurement’s ask.

Samantha — when you confirm the prompt edits we’ll run the suite and I’ll set the walkthrough invite for Thu. I’ve attached a short template for the canary playbook and the sample alert thresholds we recommend.
